features.title: Aim for close to 100% test coverage
features.description:
We need to make sure that the tests cover as close as 100% of the codebase.
Obviously, things like the ai service with getting results from the AI cannot be fully tested - but we can test for many ranges of responses by mocking the LLM responses appropriately. The same idea should be taken everywhere to try to achieve 100% coverage.

One important thing is to make sure that data that is entering and leaving endpoints is validated thoroughly to make sure that it matches the expected schema. This should be part of the code and the tests should validate it too (i.e. malformed objects being rejected).

There needs to be a relevant section in @README.md explaining how vital testing is and to refer to @docs/TESTING.md for all guidance related to writing tests and the standard for them. For reference there is also the @docs/CODE_STANDARD.md document that highlights the coding standard within the project.

features.title: Code standard
features.description:
The document @docs/CODE_STANDARD.md  highlights the overall architecture and coding standards maintained in this project.
There is a clear reference to it inside @README.md and @docs/FILE_ORGANISATION.md so that anyone creating new features or updating existing ones will go to it.
It should be as succinct as possible, but explaining the idea as well as possible.

Go over all the code and make sure that it satisfies the standards.

features.title: The environment DYNAMODB_TABLE_* names are not needed
features.description: We don't want to make the dynamodb table names configurable - they can always be completely static defined clearly somewhere within the project. The only thing the user should provide is the endpoint.

features.title: Cognito requires a secret
features.description: @src/config/configuration.ts has the 'clientSecret' added from the env. Make sure it is used for Cognito auth.

features.title: Fix the seed_database script
features.description:
Currently the @scripts/seed_database doesn't work.
The error is:


scripts/seed_database: line 60: local: `attribute-definitions=AttributeName=id,AttributeType=S': not a valid identifier

features.title: make dev/prod work via copying envs
features.description:
the run command in @package.json needs to first take the appropriate env file from `/envs` and copy it to the root of the project directory. Right now there will be `/envs/.env.dev` and `/envs/.env.prod` .
when the user calls `npm run start:dev` it needs to first copy `/envs/.env.dev` and replace the contents of it into `.env` .
when the user calls `npm run start:prod` it needs to copy `/envs/.env.prod` and replace the content of it into `.env` .
In the future we will also have a staging.

calling `npm run start` does the same as `npm run start:dev`

features.title: Create a public LLM test endpoint
features.description:
It must accept any text and feed it directly to the llm and respond in raw text back whatever it returns.
If there are any errors - throw them appropriately.
It should accept one parameter - the model type - if the correct API key is available then use the LLM - otherwise throw a meaningful error.

features.title: Generate goals
features.description:
In @src/goals/static-goals.ts there's `COMMON_GOALS` that are used throughout the app as static goals to be used whenever the service needs to provide readily available ones.
The 1st text can be made longer (up to a 100 characters) whereas the one next to it (currently blank - '') should be a summary that should be a max of 20 characters.

features.title: AI prompt needs to be improved
features.description:
Currently the `PROMPT_GOAL_SUGGESTIONS` in @src/ai/ai.service.ts doesn't specify if it's meant to be a Micro goal or Macro goal.
A Micro goal is a 'today' goal - a single shot one.
A Macro goal is a long term goal - for at least a week and usually for a month.
We need 2 prompts so that `suggestGoals` can use them accordingly (it defaults to Micro goals when type not provided).

features.title: Goals service should record the audio
features.description:
In @src/goals/goals.service.ts inside the function `suggestFromAudio` we need to record the file by uploading it to S3 and associating it with the user, so that we can analyse it later if need be.
The uploaded file in @src/goals/goals.controller.ts needs to have a size limit of 5MB.

features.title: For now, users can only set 1 macro goal at a time - no other goals are allowed
features.description: In @src/goals/goals.controller.ts and @src/goals/goals.service.ts - we need to update these so that a user can only ever have 1 MACRO goal associated with their account. In the future we might allow multiple goals of multiple types, but for now we need to make the `create` endpoint only create a goal if it's a Macro one, if it's MICRO it should throw an error. And if a user creates a new goal, it should mark the previous goal as `cancelled` (setting `completedAt` + introducing a goal state to mark when a goal is `active`, `cancelled` or `done` ). We also need an endpoint to mark the current goal as `done`.

features.title: Users can do a text or audio journal
features.description:
We need an endpoint for a user to do an audio journal and a text journal (the audio journal simply first gets transcribed) and then follows the route of the text journal.
This means that for each user there needs to be a table storing all such journals.

features.title: For each goal - we need to record the user's goal steps
features.description: A client will be able to call an endpoint on the behalf of the user, to record a UserGoalStep - a new dto to be created - that will have an id that is a reference to a user's current goal, a standard createdAt timestamp, and also a completedAt - which when created if not provided by the user gets set to the same value as createdAt. This dto also holds a reference to a @src/journals/dto/journal.dto.ts , because the user can create these goal steps in two ways - either by providing the goalId and the journalText (+ optional completedAt) or by providing an audio file, which needs to be first transcribed (similar to goals in @src/goals/goals.controller.ts ) and then follow the same path as the journalText, but also need to be recorded here.

features.title: Whenever the user submits a journal a UserMood must be recorded
features.description:
We need an appropriate prompt for an LLM to be able to try to gather the mood from a person's journal - @src/models/journal/JournalModel.dto.ts  . We first need this only text based, but we also need to prepare for the case when a user will have a more complex user profile so that can be fed into the prompt and a better mood can be decided.
If the current LLMs can do it - then when the user has provided a sound recording in the journal data then that should also be analysed for the tone of voice or any emotional load associated with the voice recording. That needs to be stored and added to the prompt with the text.  @src/models/profile/UserMoodModel.dto.ts must be used by  its own service and controller and hook in to ALL places where journals are made.

features.title: The database should auto create UUIDs and timestamps
features.description:
we should rely on standard database mechanisms for creating ids as UUIDs and timestamps (create + on any update).
This goes for any dto created by controllers - such as `Goal` via @src/goals/goals.controller.ts - that has an id, createdAt and updatedAt . Find them all and update accordingly.

features.title: All `something.interface.ts` should be removed and only `something.dto.ts` used
features.description:
In many places, such as @src/goals/goals.service.ts we use a @src/goals/interfaces/goal.interface.ts and a dto @src/goals/dto/goal.dto.ts . This creates confusion and unnecessary boilerplate as all the DTOs are identical to their interfaces.
We should remove all these `interface.ts` files and only use the `dto.ts` files which should hold all typing information needed.
Additionally, all these dto files should be placed under `src/models` as many logical places use the same file types so it doesn't make sense to bind it to a single feature.

Information about only having the DTOs should be in @docs/FILE_ORGANISATION.md and @docs/CODE_STANDARD.md

features.title: Every single endpoint should be tracked via Mixpanel

We already have @src/activity-log/activity-log.module.ts which makes @src/activity-log/activity-log.service.ts log all endpoint activities - we want to use Mixpanel to also track all events.
We also want it to track user sessions.

features.title: When transcribing audio from text - automatically get the mood/tone as well
features.description: In @src/ai/ai.service.ts when getting text out of audio by using @src/ai/transcription.service.ts  - we should also try to get the tone/mood information and it should be added into `TranscriptionResult` . The models should be moved to `src/models/ai` .

features.title: when getting free form text to process via AI - always include mood information
features.description:
When using `suggestGoals` in @src/ai/ai.service.ts , the data should also include the mood/tone information from the text input.
Whenever calling any text generation from user input - the output should include a standard mood/tone/sentiment information.

The prompts at the bottom of @src/ai/ai.service.ts should also move to @src/ai/ai-prompts.service.ts so it's easier to manage them in the future.

features.description:
We want to confirm to the user that the input was understood and send back a message like:
"You mentioned getting back into the gym and balancing that with time with your kids. Shall I record this, or do you want to re-record?"

For this to work, when the user says something about:
"I need to get back into the gym and balance that with time with my kids", we need to record that verbatim in the data but also need it summarised as:
"getting back into the gym and balancing that with time with your kids."

@src/models/ai/TranscriptionResultModel.dto.ts has a `  confirmationText` added that should be used for this purpose.
@src/ai/transcription.service.ts needs to be updated to accommodate this accordingly.

As well as the user's last completed AND not-completed micro goals, so that the new micro goals are COMPLETELY different from the last ones. The last week (so 21 micro goals) should be included in the prompt.

This calculation needs to be present on @src/models/profile/UserProfileModel.dto.ts so it's easy to get the age from this date and use it here.

features.title: New data - Momentum
features.description:
For each user we want to store some ongoing data when they keep on doing goals.
For now we need a new table that will store a new piece of data `UserMomentumModel` . Make sure this is stored and used like other pieces of data (look at @src/models/goal/GoalModel.dto.ts ).
Every user should have a momentum, we need a new controller that will be able to serve it - if a user doesn't yet have it created, then it should get created with default values.
Apart from standard id, createdAt, updatedAt, we need it to have:
- microGoalsConsecutive: number (defaults to 0), will store the number of consecutive days the user has been completing micro goals
- motivationText?: string (defaults to undefined ), this will store a motivational text that will be shown to the user.

Whenever the user records a micro goal as completed via @src/goals/goals.controller.ts - their momentum needs to be updated so that:
- the microGoalsConsecutive needs to increment if there's a day difference (date days not 24h) between the last `updatedAt` and `now`
- the motivationText needs to update depending on the number of days. For 2 or more days we need something like these texts to be set:
“You’re 2 days into your new rhythm — great start.”
    “3 days of consistency — that’s where habits start to stick.”
    “You’ve shown up 4 days in a row — real momentum now.”
    “5 days running — your consistency is building a foundation.”

Come up with a similar sounding in tone texts that we can use for up to 14 days, and then switch to showing weeks, rather than days. Have a bank of these texts for up to 4 weeks.

features.title: After the user submits a journal entry we need an acknowledgement text
features.description:
To make the user feel acknowledged we need to generate a line that will be shown to the user to make them feel heard.

The purpose of this line is light human acknowledgment, not problem-solving. It should always feel supportive but calm.

If the journal is positive: reinforce it.
    “Love that energy - you sound focused.”

If neutral: reflect consistency.
    “Sounds like a balanced day - steady progress.”

If negative: acknowledge gently without trying to fix.
    “Thanks for sharing that — small steps forward are still progress.”
or
        “That sounds like it’s been a tough stretch — great you’re ready to get back into rhythm 👊”

The goal is simply to make the user feel seen and comfortable expressing themselves.

Create an appropriate prompt for this and add a step to add this new text in @src/journals/journals.service.ts  - this text should be added to @src/models/journal/JournalModel.dto.ts when creating it. The field should be called 'acknowledgmentText'.

Create a bank of 10 supportive texts that could be used no matter what the user says in case the generation fails so that a JournalModel always contains this.

features.title: Account recovery via email/phone with Cognito ForgotPassword flow
features.description:
Goal
Enable account recovery (login) by email or phone only, with 4 endpoints that drive Cognito through AdminSetUserPassword → ForgotPassword → ConfirmForgotPassword, then authenticate and return standard tokens.

Endpoints
- POST /auth/recovery/email/initiate { email }
- POST /auth/recovery/email/confirm { email, code }
- POST /auth/recovery/phone/initiate { phoneE164 }
- POST /auth/recovery/phone/confirm { phoneE164, code }

Flow (Cognito aligned)
1) Lookup user via Cognito only (no profilesRepo):
   - email: CognitoService.findUserByEmail(email)
   - phone: CognitoService.findUserByPhoneNumber(phoneE164)
   Return username (and sub if available).
2) AdminSetUserPassword to a fixed password (e.g. 'recovery') to invalidate old creds:
   - Add helper: CognitoService.adminSetUserPassword(username, password='recovery', permanent=true)
3) ForgotPassword(username) to trigger a code via Cognito over the channel Cognito prioritises.
4) ConfirmForgotPassword(username, confirmationCode, newPassword=random-strong-password)
   - We generate a strong temporary password server-side to avoid the user picking one.
5) Authenticate with adminInitiateAuth(username, newPassword) and return LoginResultModel.

DTOs (new)
- EmailRecoveryInitiateModel { email: string }
- EmailRecoveryConfirmModel { email: string, code: string }
- PhoneRecoveryInitiateModel { phoneE164: string }
- PhoneRecoveryConfirmModel { phoneE164: string, code: string }

Service additions (AuthService)
- initiateRecoveryByEmail(email): find via Cognito, adminSetUserPassword('recovery'), forgotPassword
- confirmRecoveryByEmail(email, code): find via Cognito, confirmForgotPassword with generated strong password, adminInitiateAuth → return tokens (userId=sub)
- initiateRecoveryByPhone(phoneE164): same as email but phone lookup
- confirmRecoveryByPhone(phoneE164, code): same as email but phone lookup

Controller
- Add 4 endpoints under /auth/recovery/... mapping to the service methods; keep existing error mapping (UserNotFoundException, CodeMismatchException, ExpiredCodeException, etc.).

CognitoService additions
- adminSetUserPassword(username: string, password: string, permanent=true)
  (We already use AdminSetUserPassword in ensureUser; expose a dedicated helper.)

Security & rate limiting
- These endpoints are unauthenticated; add basic rate limits and ActivityLog entries.

Acceptance criteria
- Submitting a valid email/phone to initiate sends a code via Cognito (CODE_SENT response).
- Confirming with the correct code returns standard LoginResultModel (idToken, accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn, tokenType, userId=sub).
- Errors map to existing controller error mapping.
- If user has both email and phone, Cognito may choose the delivery channel; both endpoint types operate correctly.

Tests
- Unit tests for service and controller using a mocked CognitoService: happy paths and common errors (user not found, code mismatch, expired).

features.title: Delete account: anonymise PII and detach email/phone
features.description:
Goal
Provide an authenticated endpoint to anonymise a user account: remove personal attributes (email/phone) from Cognito to free aliases and redact corresponding fields in our profile store.

Endpoint
- DELETE /auth/account (JWT protected via Cognito access token)
  - Returns StatusModel { status: 'DELETED' } (or 'ANONYMISED').

Flow
1) Resolve current user: sub from JWT. Find Cognito username via CognitoService.findUserBySub(sub).
2) In Cognito, delete attributes so aliases can be reused:
   - AdminDeleteUserAttributes(['email','email_verified','phone_number','phone_number_verified'])
   - Add helper: CognitoService.adminDeleteUserAttributes(username: string, names: string[])
3) In profilesRepo (DynamoDB), redact PII and unlink soft references:
   - profilesRepo.updatePartial(userId=sub, { email: undefined, phoneNumber: undefined, whatsappVerified: false })
   - Optionally set a neutral display name (e.g., 'Deleted User') or other fields if present.
4) Return { status: 'DELETED' }.

Notes
- We do NOT delete the Cognito user to allow future reactivation paths if needed; we only clear aliases. If full deletion is desired later, we can add AdminDeleteUser.
- Ensure ActivityLog captures the action (but do not log PII).

CognitoService additions
- adminDeleteUserAttributes(username: string, names: string[])

Acceptance criteria
- After deletion, the same email/phone can be used to sign up/link to a different/new account.
- Profile no longer returns email/phone (and whatsappVerified=false).
- Endpoint requires a valid Cognito access token.

Tests
- Unit tests for service and controller with mocked CognitoService and profilesRepo: happy path; user not found; partial failures (rollback or best-effort logging).
